svg.text: M3.10 · Question 2: what if export.types names a type the mosaic lacks?
PR #140 · design.md View file · §5.6 (a target naming an undeclared type) · M3.5 (a wrong view file is an error naming file, line, setting)
The case: two view files for the Netflix mosaic (types Title, Person, Country, Genre, Year)
export:
types: [Title, Nope]
or
export:
types: []
Nope is not a node type of the mosaic;
[] names no type at all.
A · An error
CHOSEN: A
$ mosaic export netflix.mosaic --view v.yaml …
mosaic export: v.yaml:3: view file: export.types:
the mosaic has no node type Nope (exit 1)
• For [], the same with “export.types is empty”.
• Nothing is written.
• Like building a target that names an undeclared type (§5.6).
Why expected: a cut that names what isn't there is a
wrong view file, and M3.5 makes a wrong view file an error.
B · Carried, with a notice
$ mosaic export netflix.mosaic --view v.yaml …
netflix.mosaic: exported to export.html (exit 0)
carries Title only
• The page shows M3.6's notice: “export.types: the
mosaic has no node type Nope”.
• [] carries an empty mosaic.
A typo in a type name ships an export missing that
type; only someone opening the page sees the notice.
Not asked, for context: without export.types the export carries the mosaic as it is. The page's own types: list (what it shows)
is separate from export.types (what the file carries). A listed type that the cut lacks gets M3.6's notice (assumption 2 on the PR).
Answer on #140: Q2 A or B
